findings.description: Malformed per-kind caps can silently fall back instead of producing the documented usage error. The expression `.[$k] // ""` maps an explicit false or null to an empty string, and an explicit empty string also passes validation.
findings.failure_mode: For example, `run_usd_by_type: {build: false}` launches build trials using RUN_CAP rather than refusing the configuration. This hides a broken spend-control setting and records the fallback as the effective cap.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `has($k)` to distinguish absent entries from present values, and require every present entry to pass USD validation, including rejecting null, false, and empty strings.

findings.anchor: evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:codex token pre-flight (CODEX_PF python, required horizon)
findings.description: The pre-flight refuses any non-smoke batch whose codex access token exp is not later than now + 2 x (sum of every planned trial's watchdog_s) / concurrency. watchdog_s is already 2 x the phase sum, so the horizon is ~4 x the serial phase time / concurrency and grows linearly with the plan. Using the diff's own numbers (a1_full build watchdog 16800 s, review-catch 7200 s, 12 build + 4 review tasks, 3 trials, concurrency 3): the minimum pre-registered batch (A0, A1, A4) needs a token valid for ~15 days, and a full 8-arm batch needs ~40 days. OAuth access tokens do not live that long (ChatGPT/codex access tokens expire on the order of days), so the pre-flight will refuse the batches this runner exists to launch, and the refusal text tells the operator to `run codex login`, which cannot help because a fresh token still falls short of the horizon. There is no override flag, and the check also fires under --executor host where make_home is not used and the CLI can refresh its own token.
findings.failure_mode: Every production-size (non-smoke) batch exits 2 with REFUSED.txt `codex access token expires …, before the batch's required horizon …` regardless of how recently the operator logged in; --dry-run plan inspection is refused the same way. The cycle-130 ablation cannot be started through this runner.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the whole-batch horizon with a per-launch freshness check: before each trial launch, require exp > now + that trial's watchdog_s (plus grace) and pause/refuse only then, or warn and let the runner's existing degraded-row accounting handle expiry. At minimum: skip the check when EXECUTOR=host, add a --skip-codex-preflight (or --codex-horizon-s) override, and make the message say the batch is longer than any token lifetime rather than prescribing codex login.

findings.description: remove_colliding unlinks every candidate with a bare os.unlink(p) and then opens the sidecar .colliding-removed.txt with no exception handling. The grading tree is a copy of the agent's sandbox snapshot; if the agent left a directory without write permission (e.g. a generated read-only package dir, or a copied vendor tree), os.unlink raises PermissionError and the exception propagates out of prepare(), aborting the whole grade for that run instead of grading with the file left in place. remove_harness goes through remove_path; this new path does not reuse that helper.
findings.failure_mode: A single unwritable directory in the snapshot turns a gradeable run into a grader crash (no grade.json), which the batch runner then charges as an assumed-cap failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse remove_path (or wrap os.unlink in try/except OSError, chmod the parent u+w and retry, and record the failure in grade.json rather than raising). Treat a failed removal as a non-fatal note so the test command still runs.

findings.description: The removal walks the entire grading tree (os.walk(tree)) rather than the directories pytest will collect from, and the reserved set contains generic basenames from the fixture's tests/ dir (helpers.py, utils.py, conftest-adjacent support modules, data samples). If the sandbox snapshot contains a virtualenv, node_modules, or a vendored checkout, every site-packages module with one of those basenames is deleted and counted in colliding_tests_removed, inflating the telemetry, slowing the grade, and mutating parts of the tree that pytest never imports. pytest's import-file-mismatch only concerns modules it collects or that shadow each other on sys.path; nothing under .venv/ or .git/ is relevant.
findings.failure_mode: Bloated colliding_tests_removed counts and long grades on snapshots that include a venv or vendored tree; in refactor tasks a structural check over the final tree may see files the grader itself removed.
findings.suggested_fix: Prune the walk: skip .git, .venv/venv, node_modules, __pycache__, and site-packages directories, and ideally restrict candidates to the paths the task's test_command targets (or to directories containing collected test modules). Keep the sidecar file listing what was removed so the broader rule stays auditable.
